paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God cares about marriage, and He cares about the little ones, and Jesus shows us both in one chapter. The Pharisees wanted to argue about how much they could get away with. Jesus took them back to the beginning, where the Creator "made them male and female" and said the two "will become one flesh" (Matthew 19:4-5).

So what's the lesson on marriage? God joined them together, and Jesus says, "let man not separate" (Matthew 19:6). The Pharisees asked how little they had to keep. Jesus answered with what God meant from the start. He said Moses permitted divorce "because of your hardness of heart. But it was not this way from the beginning" (Matthew 19:8). Friend, I think that's a good question to ask my own heart: am I asking what God wants, or just what I can get away with?

Then the kids show up, and the disciples try to shoo them off. Jesus says, "Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these" (Matthew 19:14). Nobody has to be impressive to come to Jesus. So bring your questions, bring your messy heart, and come on in, baker, because when those children were brought to Him, He placed His hands on them (Matthew 19:15).
